messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — planning a short SLO-burn smoke run today to validate the ramp heuristics + heap-sampling on dedicated. Need quick thumbs and who can own profiling collection.

maria: I can take the k6 script edits and add sampling flags. What target TPS should we aim for?

alex: Target is 3k steady, with 12k burst windows for ~2m, plus a 20m soak at ~1k. Primary checks: tail latency <300ms and no OOMs. Also want to confirm heap growth <200MB over 20m.

sam: tagging infra — I can reserve a small dedicated pool (3 GPUs) and enable KV-cache warmers. Ping @ops-bot for disk iops and network knobs.

ops-bot: ops-bot: reserved pool rdp-84 for the window, baseline iops verified, no throttling expected. Will enable extended request logs -> S3 for postmortem.

jordan: For profiling I'll run async heap sampling (jemalloc + pprof). Add env var HEAP_SAMPLE=1 and capture flamegraphs every 5m. I also want to capture a one-off jemalloc dump after the burst.

alex: Here's the k6 command I'll run (can tweak):
```bash
k6 run --vus 300 --duration 20m --rps 3000 script.js --out influxdb=http://perf-db:8086
# Burst phases are handled via stages in script.js (rampTo -> hold -> rampTo down)
```

maria: I updated script.js with explicit stages and a health-gate against /internal/health. Pushed changes to perf/slo-burn.

sam: quick ask — can we run one iteration with cache prefixing off to measure cold-path latencies?

alex: yep, add header `X-Cache-Control: no-cache` to k6 requests for that iteration. Mark the run metadata as cache=disabled.

jordan: small note: set TRACE_SAMPLING=0.05 so we don't blow the tracing pipeline. Also set FLAME_INTERVAL=300 to produce 5m flame zips.

perf-bot: perf-bot: baseline snapshot uploaded -> s3://redwood-perf/baselines/1728241234.json

maria: branch pushed and PR opened (perf/slo-burn -> perf). @alex @sam pls review, just small staging changes + header flag.

sam: reviewing now — left 2 tiny nits, will approve after those. :thumbsup:

alex: ok starting smoke run in ~10m. I'll post histograms and a short summary after first 5-min window. If anything spikes we abort and roll back.

jordan: I'll have pprof + flame capture active and will upload zips to the same bucket.

alex: TEST START (run id=rdp-84-1728241234). Posting updates.

alex: 5-min update: p95 ~280ms, p99 ~420ms during the 12k burst. Heap +150MB and stable after initial ramp. No OOMs observed. Saving logs and CPU profiles to s3://redwood-perf/runs/rdp-84-1728241234/.

maria: grabbing histograms now. Running a second run with cache-disabled to compare.

sam: thanks — if p99 consistently >400ms during bursts we should open a perf-incident and consider the cpu-affinity tweak we tested last week.

alex: agreed. If the next run repeats the tail behavior we'll escalate. Tagging potential follow-ups: investigate kernel preemption, kv-cache hit skew, and quick quantization fallback. :eyes:

jordan: pushed first flame zips -> s3://redwood-perf/runs/rdp-84-1728241234/flames/. Will correlate with pprof stacks in the morning.

alex: overall good smoke. Next steps: 1) run cache-disabled iteration, 2) share histograms + flamegraphs, 3) decide on incident if repeatable. Thanks everyone for quick turn-around.
